response.sql: WITH per_item AS (SELECT order_item_id, AVG(derived_product_cost / NULLIF(derived_total_cost, 0)) AS avg_ratio, COUNT(*) AS line_item_count FROM Invoice_Line_Items GROUP BY order_item_id) SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS avg_of_avg_ratios, AVG(line_item_count) AS avg_line_item_count FROM per_item;

assumptions.assumption: A ratio is missing when derived_product_cost or derived_total_cost is NULL, or when derived_total_cost is 0 (NULLIF turns the zero into NULL so the division yields NULL). Those NULL ratios are skipped by AVG.
Each line item counts toward its order item's count whether or not its ratio is usable, because the request says to count the order item's invoice line items.
The set of order items is the distinct order_item_id values in Invoice_Line_Items, and an order item with no usable ratios drops out of the outer average of averages.

alternatives.interpretation: Count only line items that have a usable ratio, so the per-item count matches the ratios that were averaged.
alternatives.sql: WITH per_item AS (SELECT order_item_id, AVG(derived_product_cost / NULLIF(derived_total_cost, 0)) AS avg_ratio, COUNT(derived_product_cost / NULLIF(derived_total_cost, 0)) AS line_item_count FROM Invoice_Line_Items GROUP BY order_item_id) SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS avg_of_avg_ratios, AVG(line_item_count) AS avg_line_item_count FROM per_item;
